topic.title: Equivalent fractions
topic.overview: Equivalent fractions are fractions that represent the same value or proportion, even though they may have different numerators and denominators. To find equivalent fractions, multiply or divide both the numerator and denominator of a fraction by the same nonzero number. Changing only the numerator or only the denominator without the corresponding change in the other part usually changes the value of the fraction. A fraction itself denotes a ratio of the numerator to the denominator.

question.reference_answer: A fraction represents a ratio between the numerator and the denominator, where the numerator indicates how many parts of a whole or quantity are being considered, and the denominator indicates the total number of equal parts that make up the whole or the reference quantity. This ratio shows the proportion of the whole or the relationship between two quantities. For example, in the fraction 3/4, the numerator 3 means three parts are taken, and the denominator 4 means the whole is divided into four equal parts, so the fraction represents three out of four equal parts, or the ratio 3 to 4.
